tax.text: Horsford supports higher taxes on billionaires and large corporations while opposing broad tax increases on working families and small businesses.
tax.quote: I do not support across-the-board tax increases. Working families and small businesses should pay less, not more.

wages.text: Horsford introduced the TIPS Act to require a full minimum wage for tipped workers and abolish the tipped subminimum wage.
wages.quote: My bill, the TIPS Act, aims to eliminate federal (income) taxes on tips and ensure that tipped workers are paid a full minimum wage, abolishing the subminimum wage policy.

trade.text: Horsford condemned tariffs for raising consumer costs and introduced legislation to return tariff refunds to families and small businesses.
trade.quote: These illegal tariffs raised costs on everyday families and forced small businesses across the country to close their doors for good.

debt.text: Horsford backed the Social Security 2100 Act to increase benefits, protect them from inflation, and strengthen the program's finances.
debt.quote: The Social Security 2100 Act would increase Social Security benefits, protect against inflation, and modernize Social Security to ensure that government employees, caregivers, people with disabilities and surviving spouses and children receive the benefits they deserve

housing.text: Horsford supported a major housing package that expanded access to homeownership and reduced regulatory barriers.
housing.quote: Today, we are expanding access to homeownership, we are cutting red tape, and we are putting homeowners over hedge funds.

immigration.text: Horsford applauded parole-in-place and work-permit measures for undocumented family members and supported legislation protecting Dreamers.
immigration.quote: These new policies will help over 500,000 undocumented spouses and children of U.S. citizens who have lived in the country for at least ten years and have passed criminal and background checks.

cannabis.text: Horsford supported decriminalizing marijuana and preserving state-approved recreational-marijuana laws against federal interference.
cannabis.quote: I do support the state's rights and the voters in the states that have approved recreational marijuana to allow their rights to be upheld and that the federal government needs to stay out of it

health.text: Horsford advocated restoring Affordable Care Act subsidies and protecting Medicaid from cuts.
health.quote: House Democrats will never stop fighting to restore the enhanced ACA tax credits, protect Medicaid, and lower costs for every Nevadan.

voting.text: Horsford helped introduce the John R. Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act to restore federal protections against discriminatory voting restrictions.
voting.quote: On August 17, 2021, Congressman Steven Horsford joined Congresswoman Terri Sewell and more than 190 members of Congress to introduce H.R. 4, the John R. Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act.

tax.text: Whipple says lower taxes, lighter regulation, and domestic energy production would reduce household costs.
tax.quote: Lower taxes, lighter regulation, and domestic energy production keep costs down, while government-mandated inflation eats away at household paychecks.

trade.text: Described himself as supportive of free markets while also supporting tools to protect American workers and promote fair trade.
trade.quote: "We have all felt the pressure from tariffs," Whipple wrote. "I believe in the free market, but also want to protect American and Nevada workers, and fair trade.

debt.text: Whipple's campaign says Medicaid and Social Security should be protected by eliminating waste, fraud, and abuse.
debt.quote: Eliminate waste, fraud, and abuse to protect this vital safety net.

housing.text: Whipple said he supports the Clark County lands bill, which would open land for affordable housing and new jobs while protecting conservation areas.

schools.text: Whipple describes himself as a strong advocate for school choice, career education, and expanded youth sports.
schools.quote: He is a strong advocate for school choice, career and technical education, and expanding youth sports opportunities to ensure every child has the chance to succeed.

safety.text: Whipple rejects defunding police and says law-enforcement officers and first responders should receive the resources needed to do their jobs.
safety.quote: Our law enforcement officers and first responders deserve a representative in Washington who will listen to them, stand up for them, and make sure they have the resources they need to do their jobs.

immigration.text: Supported deporting undocumented immigrants who committed serious felonies first while favoring exceptions for certain minors, students and family circumstances.
immigration.quote: Whipple wrote that he supports exceptions for those younger than 18, students "currently enrolled in college with good records" and "families who have immediate members like a spouse or minor children in the country legally."

guns.text: Whipple says he believes in protecting Second Amendment rights and supports firearm-safety education.
guns.quote: A lifelong sportsman and conservationist, Cody has worked closely with wildlife organizations and believes in protecting Second Amendment rights.

energy.text: Whipple supports domestic energy production as a way to keep household costs down.
energy.quote: Lower taxes, lighter regulation, and domestic energy production keep costs down, while government-mandated inflation eats away at household paychecks.

voting.text: Whipple praised a proposal for mandatory national voter identification.
voting.quote: The President’s support for mandatory national voter ID reflects a commitment to protecting the integrity of our elections.
